conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the claim is false and concludes that claims of dangerous CO2 buildup from prolonged mask use lack support and are contradicted by credible research.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
## Conclusion

The claim that prolonged cloth/surgical mask use causes *dangerous* CO2 buildup is **false**. While masks do cause a small, measurable rise in inhaled CO2, credible peer-reviewed research and fact-checks consistently find this rise is far below levels that cause harm (hypercapnia) in healthy individuals.

## Evidence

Multiple controlled studies measuring CO2 directly under masks found only modest increases that remained within safe physiological limits. A study in *Aerosol and Air Quality Research* found face masks caused some CO2 elevation but concluded it did not reach hazardous levels for healthy wearers (https://aaqr.org/articles/aaqr-20-07-covid-0403). Similarly, a *BMC Infectious Diseases* study of healthcare workers wearing masks/respirators for extended periods found CO2 "remains below" clinically concerning thresholds (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12879-021-06056-0). A related clinical trial on medical masks plus N95-equivalent respirators worn for 2-hour ED shifts found changes "clinically insignificant" and concluded it is safe for healthy healthcare workers (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35058098/).

Fact-checkers reinforce this: USA Today, citing physiology experts, states "it is unlikely that wearing a mask will cause hypercapnia," and notes viral claims of hypoxia/hypercapnia from masks have been repeatedly debunked (https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/05/30/fact-check-wearing-face-mask-not-cause-hypoxia-hypercapnia/5260106002/). Notably, a widely-cited JAMA Pediatrics paper claiming dangerous CO2 buildup in children's masks was retracted shortly after publication due to methodological flaws (https://retractionwatch.com/author/ivanoransky/page/33/), undermining a key source often used to support the false claim.

**Bottom line:** Masks cause small, physiologically insignificant increases in inhaled CO2 in healthy people; claims of dangerous buildup lack support from properly conducted studies and rely partly on retracted or flawed research.
